author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Yemen’s Houthi forces have seized the southwestern port city of Mocha after a rapid advance along the Red Sea coast, strengthening their position near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.

Reuters reported that Yemeni government, Iranian and regional sources described direct guidance from Iran’s Revolutionary Guards during the campaign. Two Iranian sources said Tehran had urged the Houthis to increase attacks on Saudi Arabia and offered additional funding, weapons and senior officers.

Iran publicly rejects descriptions of the Houthis as a proxy. One Iranian official told Reuters that the decision to move on Mocha was the group’s own, while acknowledging that the advance increased pressure on oil markets and on U.S. and Saudi interests.

Control around Bab el-Mandeb matters because the narrow waterway connects the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and is a major route for shipping and energy cargoes. The reported seizure is a developing military and trade-route risk. Independent access to the battlefield is limited, and claims about command arrangements rely on the sources cited by Reuters.
dek: Sources told Reuters that Iranian guidance and weapons supported a rapid coastal advance that strengthened the group’s position near Bab el-Mandeb.
headline: Houthi seizure of Mocha tightens pressure on Red Sea route
